content.summary: The request was to add a zoomed-in version of Figure 1 covering x in [1.6, 3.3] with the matching y range. The work does this without changing what was asked. The new figure keeps both panels of the original D-vs-W scatter (block 18 and block 35) with the same markers. The x-axis is limited to D from 1.6 to 3.3. Each panel's y-axis runs from the smallest to the largest W among tokens in that D range, which is the natural reading of 'the corresponding y range'. The y limits in the image match the ones stated in the caption (block 18: 0.065–0.627, block 35: 0.021–0.650), with a small padding. Both axes are labelled. The original Figure 1 is unchanged, and the zoom is added right after it as Figure 2. It has a short sentence explaining why it is there, a caption naming both axes and the limits, and it says which tokens the zoom leaves out (9 with D < 1.6, 19 with D between 3.3 and 4, and the 64-token group at D ≈ 5.17). Later figures are renumbered consistently. The new text makes only descriptive claims ('no clear slope', 'spread at fixed D much larger than change across D'), and the median values in the report back these up. It makes no causal or mechanistic claims. The report is still short, well under the 5,000-word limit, with 4 of the allowed 8 main figures, and it stays focused on the core question. Nothing was added beyond the requested figure. Minor note: the flagged points are hard to tell apart as crosses at this marker size, but the legend explains the markers.
